purpose: Authoritative identity and version-source catalog for products and plugins in the A.S.F.R.E.E ecosystem.

plugins.source_activation_rule: Only a reviewed commit merged into main is active. A branch or unmerged pull-request candidate is not the active canonical release.
plugins.change_history_source: CHANGELOG.md and Git commit history; Plugin Creator release metadata is a deployment record and must be reconciled by read-back.

plugins.version_source: Plugin Creator release metadata for this exact plugin ID
plugins.source_activation_rule: The redirect package's own release version identifies only the compatibility shell; it does not identify or pin the A.S.F.R.E.E product version.
plugins.change_history_source: This package's CHANGELOG.md and immutable Plugin Creator release history.

independent_artifacts.version_source: Mirrors plugin/plugin.json; no independent version authority.
Mirrors plugin/plugin.json; no independent version authority.
Plugin Creator release metadata for the canonical plugin ID.
Each bundle's versioned filename and adjacent SHA-256 sidecar.

products.change_history_source: CHANGELOG.md and Git commit history for source changes; Plugin Creator release history plus verified read-back for deployed plugin releases.

global_invariants: Each product_id has exactly one registered plugin with role CANONICAL.
Every plugin identity has one stable identity_id, one unique Plugin Creator plugin_id, one name, one declared version_source, and one change_history_source.
Every COMPATIBILITY_REDIRECT targets exactly one CANONICAL plugin within the same product.
Only the canonical package manifest in the reviewed main branch determines the active canonical package SemVer.
Unmerged branches and pull-request candidates are not active releases.
Plugin Creator release IDs are deployment identifiers; deployment metadata and file read-back must match the reviewed source package before synchronization is claimed.
Compatibility manifests and package READMEs mirror the canonical manifest and are not independent version authorities.
A compatibility redirect's own SemVer applies only to that redirect package and must not pin or redefine the canonical product SemVer.
A redirect never falls back to a superseded implementation when its canonical destination is unavailable.
Runtime and source-bundle versions remain independent artifact version planes.
